title: The graph-exceptional-fibre construction of the relative nodal branch scheme
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Write $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ for its first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Let $s=(i,1_D):D\to X\times_T D$ be the graph, formed by [def-pc-fibre-product]. This graph is an immersion: its composite with the first projection is the closed immersion $i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and immersions have the cancellation property. Let $W$ be the canonical open coborder neighbourhood of its image, so that $s$ factors as a closed immersion $j:D\hookrightarrow W$ followed by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. With $J=\ker(\mathcal O_W\to j_*\mathcal O_D)$, form the global blow-up $b:\operatorname{Bl}_J(W)\to W$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Define $B_f=\operatorname{Bl}_J(W)\times_W D$ and $p_f:B_f\to D$ to be the second projection. Thus $B_f$ is the relative Proj over $D$ of the ideal-power quotients $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}J^n/J^{n+1}$. On affine graph neighbourhoods this is the projectivized graph tangent cone, independently of the chosen neighbourhood; the coborder gives a fixed real construction, including for nonseparated families. No nodal, flatness, properness or nonemptiness hypothesis is used to define these objects.
